newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, Estonia eye stock depository deal - agency.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, Estonia eye stock depository deal - agency.

text.p: The Latvian and Estonian central securities depositories are to sign this month a deal to allow the registration of both countries' shares at each depository, news agency the Baltic News Service (BNS) said on Thursday.
It quoted officials as saying that the agreement would be signed on January 31.
The central depository of Lithuania had not shown any interest in taking part in the new system, the agency added.
Local market players say that a joint depository would allow cross-border share trading to become easier and boost the stock markets.
Estonia's bourse is the newest, having started in May 1996 while Latvia's bourse opened in mid-1995. Lithuania has had a stock market since late 1993.
Volumes on all three bourses have been rising as the yields and profits that can be earned on government paper in the Baltics and elsewhere in eastern Europe have fallen.
